components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time

## Summary

I implemented optional owner `email` support end-to-end, following the existing `telephone` conventions in this Spring Boot app.

**Changes:**

1. **`openapi.yml`** — Added an optional `email` property to the `OwnerFields` schema with `format: email` and `minLength/maxLength`. Because `performBeanValidation` is enabled, the generator emits `@jakarta.validation.constraints.Email` on the request DTO, so a present-but-invalid address (e.g. `not-an-email`) is rejected with **400** by the existing validation advice.

2. **`model/Owner.java`** — Added the `email` field (`@Column(name="email")`) with getter/setter.

3. **`mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — Added a `normalizeEmail` mapping that lower-cases the address on the create path (mirroring `normalizeTelephone`), so it's stored and returned lower-cased.

4. **`controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — The update path also lower-cases email via `ownerMapper.normalizeEmail(...)`, keeping create and update consistent.

5. **DB schemas** — Added an `email VARCHAR(255)`/`TEXT` column to `owners` in all four schema files (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres); tests use `ddl-auto=none` so the column must exist in SQL. I also converted the hsqldb `data.sql` owner seed inserts to use an explicit column list, since positional `INSERT ... VALUES` broke once a column was added (the other dialects already named columns).

The three acceptance tests — lower-casing a mixed-case email, rejecting an invalid one with 400, and accepting a missing email — all pass, as does the rest of the suite.
